title: Spean Thma
visualBrief: Spean Thma ruin with stepped sandstone corbels, projecting moss-stained pier bases, displaced paving and a low broken eastern apron. Two intertwining trees retain the pale low fork and the rooted dark trunk.
nativeAxes: +X east-northeast; -X west-southwest; +Z south-southeast toward the nearby modern road; -Z north-northwest.

sourceFacts.identity: The named Spean Thmor point and south-side photographs identify the ruin. Eight bays represent the central visible stretch. An additional broken paving apron interprets the continuation seen in the wider gallery photo. The exact surviving endpoints and bearing remain approximate.

approximateReconstruction.southPierAprons: Six distinct stepped bases interpret the foreground stones in the 2025 south-side reference. The adjacent corbel passages stay open.

sourceFacts.orientationReview: The ruin’s east–west axis follows the adjoining Petit Circuit approach as a local alignment proxy. The photographed corbel openings and two tree roots face toward the geotagged southwest viewpoint. The point location comes from the named PMTiles feature. The full surviving extent and the exact compass bearing remain approximate.

references.author: Ken Marshall
references.use: Inspected south-side photo: knotted pale tree forks low over the front broken masonry; a taller dark tree stands behind on retained paving. Three central corbel openings and broken outer block courses. Camera GPS13.446008/103.879483 supports the named ruin identity and south-facing interpretation; it does not give a measured heading.

references.author: TravelSafe BC
references.use: Inspected frontal image of low fork, roots wrapping/descending over irregular piers, taller dark tree and collapsed lateral channels. No pixels imported; full ends remain cropped.

references.use: Inspected public wider photo before a registration prompt appeared: root-covered collapsed piers extend beyond the narrower intact-section photographs. Roots creep horizontally across multiple stone courses before descending; a further rooted tree stands on the broken section. Current draft does not yet cover that full remnant.

references.use: Inspected close view of three squared corbel passages, massive roots above the paving, irregular courses and broken outer masonry.
Front photograph shows uneven pier heads, stepped sandstone courses, dark moss staining, and the two rooted trunks at different elevations. Ordinary view of the photographed central section.

limitations: The mapped Spean Thmor point and geotagged south-facing photographs establish the ruin’s vicinity. The exact axis and all surviving masonry beyond the known views remain unverified.

Six central passages are partially roofed. The broken eastern apron interprets the continuation visible in a wider photograph. Individual block positions, hidden foundations and the full surviving bay schedule remain estimates.
The two trees use photo-led root paths, irregular bark profiles and modeled foliage. Both mapped modern crossings are independent of the ruin.
